---
title: "R for Survey Data"
subtitle: "Weights, design-based estimates, and regression with the National Health Interview Survey (NHIS)"
---

National surveys like the NHIS do not sample people at random from the whole population. To describe the population correctly, every analysis must account for the survey's **weights** and **design**. These lessons teach that, using the 2025 NHIS Sample Adult file.

**Running example:** among adults who have had cancer, how does self-rated health differ by socioeconomic position?

| [N1: Meet the NHIS](https://colab.research.google.com/github/icohr-lab/tutorials/blob/main/notebooks/N1_Meet_the_NHIS.ipynb) | Colab | Codebooks, loading the data, refused/don't-know codes | Ready |
| [N2: Preparing Variables](https://colab.research.google.com/github/icohr-lab/tutorials/blob/main/notebooks/N2_Preparing_Variables.ipynb) | Colab | Recoding to `NA`, analysis variables, checking against the codebook | Ready |
| [N3: Moving to RStudio](n3-rstudio.qmd) | RStudio | Installing R and RStudio, projects, scripts | Ready |
| N4: Why Weights Matter | RStudio | Weighted vs. unweighted estimates, the survey design object | Planned |
